intent: TEST for PipelineSubscriptions. Write JUnit 5 + AssertJ tests (StepVerifier for reactive types, Mockito for collaborators, WebTestClient for controllers) asserting ONLY the ast_hints API and the invariants below; cover happy paths, boundaries and error cases. Context: event bridge between contexts (Intake -> Chronology Reconciliation -> Ledger). Implements org.springframework.context.SmartLifecycle. Constructor PipelineSubscriptions(BoundedEventChannel<TelemetryContracts.TelemetrySampleValidated> validatedChannel, BoundedEventChannel<TelemetryContracts.TelemetrySampleValidationFailed> failedChannel, ReconcileChronologyUseCase reconcile, BoundedEventChannel<TelemetryContracts.TelemetrySampleOrdered> orderedChannel, BoundedEventChannel<TelemetryContracts.TelemetryBackfillDetected> backfillChannel, AppendTelemetryRecordUseCase append). start(): idempotent; subscribes four pipelines, each with concatMap so ordering is preserved and demand is bounded: validated -> reconcile(sample, VALID); failed -> reconcile(sample, VALIDATION_FAILED); ordered -> append.appendOrdered; backfill -> append.appendBackfill. A per-event error is logged and swallowed (onErrorResume) so one bad event never cancels a subscription. stop(): idempotent; non-blocking: runs reconcile.flush() then disposes all subscriptions once flush completes. isRunning() reflects the started state. Subscriptions are owned and disposed here (no leaks).
